compile.globalConstraints:
- No engine, boot, launcher, janitor, client or kernel changes: the probe is a new file beside the sims, the exam a new sim, and the rest is prose in three documents.
- The probe is never a suite member: its name begins `probe_`, `tests/test_fleet_suite.py` globs only `test_*.mjs`, and the new exam is a `test_*.mjs` that reaches the probe by `import` against an in-memory fake transport — no process spawned, no network, no file read outside the checkout and the temp dir.
- No bearer on the laptop, ever: every request the probe makes rides `fleet/kata-client.mjs`'s `sshTransport` (the remote string carries the literal `$KATA_AUTH_TOKEN`, expanded on the hub), and the probe never reads `KATA_TOKEN` from `~/.ultrapowers/kata-hub.env` — only `KATA_URL`'s host.
- Every sim keeps printing `ALL TESTS PASSED` on its last line and names no sibling sim.
- A sibling plan (bundle B, authored the same sitting) may edit other sections of `fleet/CONTRACT.md`; this plan's edits to that file are confined to the kata paragraph and the new list bullet, so a same-file fold with that run is line-disjoint.

llmDerives: waves[][].tier on the args-file wave entries (slots pre-emitted as null; the engine reads knobs ONLY from these inline entries — never a top-level launch key)

nothing for waves[][].testCmd — the per-task command is compiler-derived from the task's Proof `Test:` paths and pre-filled on the wave entries (run-wide testCmd is driver-derived — knob or detection — and already stamped in the args file and receipt)

nothing for bootstrapCmd — driver-derived from the target's lockfile/manifest (or the --bootstrap-cmd knob) and stamped in the args file and receipt, so validation, the engine and the gate share one value
nothing for review depth — it is plan-authored (**Review:** marker), pre-filled on the args wave entries
